sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Context**: The **Communal Award (1932)** by Ramsay MacDonald granted separate electorates to the Depressed Classes, which Gandhi viewed as a 'vivisection' of the Hindu community.
• **Mechanism**: Gandhi undertook a **'Fast Unto Death'** at Yerwada Jail, Pune, to protest the political segregation of Dalits.
• **Resolution**: The Pact replaced separate electorates with **Joint Electorates** but significantly increased the number of reserved seats for the Depressed Classes.
• **Key Metric**: Reserved seats for the Depressed Classes in the Provincial Legislatures were increased from 71 (under the Communal Award) to 148.

sections.title: Comprehensive Classification & Comparative Matrix
rows: Separate electorates for Depressed Classes; 71 seats.
British 'Divide and Rule' policy to weaken nationalist movement.
Joint electorates; 148 seats; representation in Central Legislature.
Compromise between Gandhi's unity goal and Ambedkar's political empowerment goal.
Mains: Impact on Dalit political trajectory.

items.definition: A system where all voters, regardless of caste, vote for a candidate, but the candidate must belong to the reserved category.
The term used in the 1930s to refer to the marginalized sections of society, later categorized as Scheduled Castes.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **Political Integration**: Ensured Dalits remained part of the Hindu political fold while securing legislative presence.
• **Social Reform**: Triggered the formation of the All India Anti-Untouchability League (later Harijan Sevak Sangh).

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Challenges**: Critics argue it diluted the political autonomy of Dalits by making them dependent on general voters.
• **Solutions**: Post-independence constitutional safeguards (Articles 330, 332) evolved from this framework.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'P-A-C-T' (Pune, Ambedkar, Communal Award, Total Seats increased).
• **Decoded Meaning**: P (Pune/Yerwada), A (Ambedkar-Gandhi), C (Communal Award reaction), T (Total seats 71 to 148).

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often states that the Poona Pact was signed by Gandhi. Technically, Gandhi was in jail; the pact was signed by Madan Mohan Malaviya and others on his behalf, though with his full consent.
Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Political Empowerment vs. Social Integration' to analyze the debate between Ambedkar and Gandhi.

keyTakeaways: The Poona Pact ended the threat of separate electorates for Dalits.
It established the principle of reserved seats in joint electorates, which remains the basis for SC/ST representation in India today.
It marked a shift in the nationalist movement towards addressing the 'untouchability' issue as a core political priority.
